children.translated_text: Having bowed according to proper rite at the lotus feet of the guru, who is the cause of attaining the state of glorious <s>Vajrasattva</s>,

children.text: tatparyupāstiramalā bahutantragītā saṃkṣipya kathyata iyaṃ śṛṇutādareṇa // 1 //
children.translated_text: his pure service, celebrated in many <s>tantras</s>, is now briefly told — listen with reverence. || 1 ||
For the <s>vajrācārya</s> (vajra-master), foremost among the consecrated (<s>abhiṣeka</s>), by the <s>Tathāgatas</s>
dwelling in the world-realms of the ten directions, having approached across the three times, is venerated. || 2 ||
Three times [daily], with supreme devotion, with offerings of flowers, joined palms, and <s>maṇḍalas</s>,
the guru, the teacher, should be worshipped through the bowing of the head at [his] feet. || 3 ||

children.text: saddharmādīn puraskṛtya gṛhī vā navako 'pi vā /
children.translated_text: One who upholds the true <s>Dharma</s> and the rest, whether a householder or even a novice,
should be honored with wisdom by vow-holders, for the removal of worldly blame. || 4 ||
Offering a comfortable seat, rising [in his presence], showing respect in actions and so forth —
all this a vow-holder (<s>vratī</s>) should do, setting aside [only formal] worship and salutation. || 5 ||
Before [entering] the teacher-student relationship, the wise should examine [each other];
for the downfall from a shared <s>samaya</s> (vow) is a fault for both guru and disciple. || 6 ||
One who is merciless, wrathful, cruel, haughty, fickle, and unrestrained,

children.text: svotkarṣakaṃ ca no kuryād guruṃ śiṣyaṃ ca buddhimān // 7 //
children.translated_text: and one who exalts himself — the wise one should make neither such a guru nor such a disciple. || 7 ||
Steadfast, disciplined, intelligent, patient, upright, honest,
knowledgeable in the practice of <s>mantras</s> and <s>tantras</s>, compassionate, learned in the scriptures, || 8 ||
fully knowing the ten <s>tattvas</s> (principles), skilled in <s>maṇḍala</s>-drawing rites,
an expounder of <s>mantras</s> — such a master should be serene and with controlled senses. || 9 ||

children.text: taṃ nāthaṃ yo 'vamanyeta śiṣyo bhūtvā sacetanaḥ /
children.translated_text: That conscious student who, having become a disciple, disrespects that lord —
by [such] contempt of all <s>Buddhas</s>, he would forever experience suffering. || 10 ||
Through calamities, disasters, thieves, planetary afflictions, fevers, poisons, and the like,
that greatly deluded one who reviles the guru's feet dies. || 11 ||
By kings, storms, fires, serpents, <s>ḍākinīs</s>, floods, robbers,
and by obstructing <s>Vināyakas</s> — slain [by these], he goes to hell. || 12 ||
One should never agitate the mind of the master;

children.text: yadā karoti duṣprajño narake pacyate dhruvam // 13 //
children.translated_text: when the foolish one does so, he is surely cooked in hell. || 13 ||
The hells that have been described — <s>Avīci</s> and others, terrifying —

children.text: tatra vāsaḥ samākhyāta ācāryasya hi nindanāt // 14 //
children.translated_text: dwelling therein is declared [the result] of reviling the master. || 14 ||
Therefore, with every effort, the great guru, the <s>vajrācārya</s> (vajra-master),
whose excellent virtues are concealed, should never be disrespected. || 15 ||
Through the giving of whatever offering is desired, [showing] devotion and respect to the guru,

children.text: uktā jvarādayastāpā na bhūyaḥ prabhavanti hi // 16 //
children.translated_text: the previously mentioned afflictions such as fevers will no longer prevail. || 16 ||
With what cannot [ordinarily] be given — one's own sons, wife, and so forth, or even one's own life —
one should serve one's own <s>saṃvara</s>-master; how much more so with transient wealth! || 17 ||
For that which is extremely difficult to obtain even in countless millions of <s>kalpas</s> —
<s>Buddhahood</s> — [the guru] gives to the diligent one in this very lifetime. || 18 ||
One should always practice one's own <s>samaya</s> (vow), always worship the <s>Tathāgatas</s>,

children.text: nityaṃ ca gurave deyaṃ sarvabuddhasamo hyasau // 19 //
children.translated_text: and always give to the guru — for he is equal to all <s>Buddhas</s>. || 19 ||
Whatever is most cherished in the world, or even more excellent —
all that should be given to the guru by one who ever desires the inexhaustible. || 20 ||
By giving to him, one gives to all <s>Buddhas</s> for eternity;
and from that comes the accumulation of merit (<s>puṇya-saṃbhāra</s>), and from that accumulation, supreme <s>Bodhi</s> (enlightenment). || 21 ||
Those disciples who are endowed with the virtues of compassion, renunciation, moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), and patience (<s>kṣānti</s>),
and who do not imagine any difference between the guru and <s>Vajradhara</s> — || 22 ||
even out of fear of [the sin of] breaking a <s>caitya</s> (shrine) and the like, one should not step over the guru's shadow;
how much less should one step over his shoes, seat, vehicle, and the like! || 23 ||
The great-minded one should listen joyfully and attentively to the guru's command;
if unable [to fulfill it], he should explain to him his inability with good reason. || 24 ||

children.text: guroḥ siddhiṃ samāpnoti guroḥ svargaṃ guroḥ sukham /
children.translated_text: From the guru comes <s>siddhi</s> (attainment), from the guru comes heaven, from the guru comes happiness;
therefore, with every effort, one should never transgress the guru's command. || 25 ||
One should regard the guru's property as one's own self, and his wife as the guru [herself],
and his people as one's own relatives — always with mindful attention. || 26 ||
One should not mount [the guru's] bed, [take] the foremost vehicle, bind on a turban and the like [in his presence];

children.text: na kuryādāsane pādaṃ kaṭihastaṃ ca sannidhau // 27 //
children.translated_text: one should not put one's foot on [his] seat, nor stand with hands on hips in his presence. || 27 ||

children.text: suptena vā niṣaṇṇena na stheyamutthite gurau /
children.translated_text: When the guru has risen, one should not remain lying down or sitting;
one should always be skillful and diligent in performing his tasks. || 28 ||
The discarding of phlegm and the like, stretching out one's legs, likewise

children.text: caṅkramaṇaṃ vivādaṃ ca na kuryāt purato guroḥ // 29 //
children.translated_text: walking about, and arguing — one should not do [these] in front of the guru. || 29 ||

children.text: saṃvāhanaṃ nartanaṃ ca na gānaṃ na ca bādanam /
children.translated_text: Massaging, dancing, singing, and playing [music] —

children.text: bahu saṃlapanaṃ cāpi na kuryāt purato guroḥ // 30 //
children.translated_text: and excessive chattering — one should not do in the presence of the <s>guru</s>. // 30 //
Having bowed, one should rise from the seat and sit down again with devotion.

children.text: niśyapsu sabhaye mārge prārthyāgre gamanaṃ caret // 31 //
children.translated_text: At night, on dangerous paths, one should request to walk ahead [of the <s>guru</s>]. // 31 //

children.text: nāṅgāni cālayed dhīmān na jṛmbhādi samāśrayet /
children.translated_text: The wise one should not fidget with the limbs, nor indulge in yawning and the like,
nor crack the knuckles in the presence of the teacher who is watching. // 32 //
Washing of the feet, wiping the body, anointing, and massaging —

children.text: pūrvaṃ praṇamya kartavyaṃ tataḥ kuryād yadādiśet // 33 //
children.translated_text: having first bowed down, these should be performed; then one should do whatever [the <s>guru</s>] commands. // 33 //
[When invoking the <s>guru</s>'s name on occasions of invitation and the like, one should prefix honorifics such as '<s>pūjyapāda</s>' (venerable);
at other times, one should speak with faith and with respectful epithets. // 34 //
'Please command, I shall carry it out' — thus one should address the <s>guru</s> with joined palms.
Having heard the command and without wavering, one should act exactly as instructed. // 35 //
When laughter or a cough arises, one should cover the mouth with the hand.
After that, in gentle words, one should convey one's intention. // 36 //
One should be humble in the <s>guru</s>'s presence, properly dressed with garments well-fastened,

children.text: bhūjānuḥ sāñjaliḥ śrotuṃ yācayet tu trivārakam // 37 //
children.translated_text: kneeling with joined palms; one should request to listen three times. // 37 //
One should always perform meritorious deeds with a mind free from ego,
restrained with modesty and fear of sin, like a newly-wed bride. // 38 //

children.text: na vilāsamayīṃ ceṣṭāṃ kuryāt śāstari saṃmukhe /
children.translated_text: One should not perform coquettish or frivolous actions in the teacher's presence;
and other such conduct of this kind, having carefully examined [it], one should firmly abandon. // 39 //

children.text: pratiṣṭhāyāṃ maṇḍale ca home vā śiṣyasaṃgrahe /
children.translated_text: At consecrations (<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>), in the <s>maṇḍala</s> [ritual], in <s>homa</s> (fire offerings), in gathering of disciples,
at the beginning of teachings, and in the <s>guru</s>'s dwelling — one should always maintain [the <s>guru</s>'s] presence. // 40 //
Whatever is obtained at consecrations and the like, all that should be offered to the <s>guru</s>;

children.text: tena dattaṃ ca gṛṇhīyāt svayaṃ cānyāṃśca toṣayet // 41 //
children.translated_text: what is given by him should be accepted, and one should also please others [with it]. // 41 //
One should never establish one's own discipleship over the <s>guru</s>'s disciple;
one should keep one's own disciple restrained from [receiving] honors and the like in the <s>guru</s>'s presence. // 42 //

children.text: ācāryo yatsvayaṃ dadyād gururvā yat pradāpayet /
children.translated_text: Whatever the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) gives of his own accord, or whatever the <s>guru</s> causes to be given,
that should be received by the wise one, having bowed down, with cupped palms joined together. // 43 //
Being ever mindful, diligently performing all observances toward one's own kinsmen,
one should dismiss the unmindful with affection and a joyful heart. // 44 //
If one who has been permitted does not faithfully carry out the <s>guru</s>'s task,

children.text: rugṇastu kuśale citte naivaṃ bhavati pāpabhāk // 45 //
children.translated_text: but is ill and has a wholesome mind, such a one does not incur sin. // 45 //
What more [need be said]? One should do whatever is possible to please the <s>guru</s>;
the observances should be performed with effort; one should never disregard [them]. // 46 //
In every way, at all times, <s>siddhi</s> (spiritual attainment) follows the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher);
the <s>guru</s>, by the word of <s>Vajradhara</s>, is to be propitiated with all offerings. // 47 //

children.text: śiṣyaḥ śuddhāśayo bhūtvā triratnaṃ śaraṇaṃ vrajet /
children.translated_text: The disciple, having become pure in intention, should take refuge in the <s>Triratna</s> (Three Jewels);
having studied under the <s>guru</s>, one should recite [the teachings] and also perform the concluding rite (<s>utsarga</s>). // 48 //
Then, through the bestowal of <s>mantras</s> and the like, having been made a vessel of the true <s>Dharma</s>,
one should recite, retain, and [observe] the fourteen root transgressions (<s>mūlāpatti</s>). // 49 //
For the disciple who follows the <s>guru</s>, who is faultless, having accomplished the increase of all welfare — whatever merit I have accumulated by this [work],

children.text: kuśalapadamanantaṃ tena vai sarvasatvāḥ vijitasugatabhāvā drāk susiddhiṃ labheyuḥ // 50 //
children.translated_text: by that, may all beings, having attained the state of the victorious <s>Sugata</s> (Buddha), swiftly obtain supreme <s>siddhi</s> (attainment). // 50 //

body.translated_text: // Thus the <s>Gurupañcāśikā</s> (Fifty Verses on the Guru) is concluded. //
// This is the composition of the great <s>ācārya</s> <s>Aśvaghoṣa</s>. //
